messages.content: 尋找紐約附近提供素食選項的義大利餐廳，以及洛杉磯提供外送服務的日本壽司餐廳。

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find restaurants. They want:

- In New York (NY) near them, Italian restaurants that provide vegetarian options.
- In Los Angeles (LA), Japanese sushi restaurants that provide delivery service.

We need to use the function restaurant_finder. The function signature: restaurant_finder({location: string, cuisine: string, preferences?: ...}). The preferences can be "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[].

We need to call the function twice: one for New York Italian vegetarian, one for Los Angeles Japanese delivery.

We need to produce a function call. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we should call the function twice. But the function can only be called once? The function signature expects a single call. But we can call it twice. The system might allow multiple calls. We can do two separate calls. The user wants two sets of results. So we can call the function twice.

We need to produce JSON calls. The assistant should output the function calls. According to guidelines, we should not output any additional text. Just the function calls. But we can output them sequentially. The assistant can call the function twice. The function calls should be in JSON format. The assistant should not output any explanation. Just the function calls.

Thus we produce:

{
  "name": "restaurant_finder",
  "arguments": {
    "location": "New York, NY",
    "cuisine": "Italian",
    "preferences": ["Vegetarian"]
  }
}

Then second call:

{
  "name": "restaurant_finder",
  "arguments": {
    "location": "Los Angeles, CA",
    "cuisine": "Japanese",
    "preferences": ["Delivery"]
  }
}

But the function signature says preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[], so preferences can be an array. So we pass array.

Thus we produce two calls.
